newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Hambros to see first half upturn.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Hambros to see first half upturn.

text.p: British merchant bank Hambros Plc is expected to report improved first-half results next week, but analysts have yet to be convinced of its long-term prospects.

"It will show a big turnaround in its estate agency business (Hambro Countrywide ), but it is not going to see the same upturn in its banking side," one analyst, who declined to be named, told Reuters on Friday.

And it will be difficult for the bank, currently under fire from Hong Kong investment manager Regent Pacific Group, which holds three percent of the firm, to acheive greater profitability in a fiercely competitive market place, he added.
Analysts forecast that Hambros will report pre-tax profits of 45.0 million stg for the half-year and declare an interim dividend of between 2.5 and 3.0 pence per share.
This compares with a pre-tax loss of 7.7 million stg and an interim dividend of 2.5 pence for the same period last year when Hambros reported a bad debt charge of 23.5 million stg.
When it reported its full year results, Hambros said it had been strict in provisioning and believed its total loan book to be "prudently valued".
Analysts said they assumed the full year provisioning of 36.2 million stg for the year would not be repeated.
Hambros made a pre-tax profit of 20.6 million stg and paid a 7.5 pence total dividend for the year to March 31.
Analysts said Regent, which has said it wants to break up Hambros to realise shareholder value, will not force any radical changes to the bank's strategy in the short-term.
Regent wants the bank to sell its 51 percent holding in Hambro Countrywide, which has returned to profit following an upturn in the hitherto depressed British property market.
The British estate agency and financial products group reported pre-tax profits for the first half of the year of 10.5 million stg, compared with a loss of 5.8 million stg.
"I don't really think Regent changes things too much. This is a company which knows that it needs to get its returns up," another analyst said.
And while there was no easy way for Hambros to improve its profitability, the bank remains one of the least likely takeover target for acquisitive global investment banks, he added.
